entries.title: New Composer UI, Agent, Commit Messages
entries.titleJa: Cursor 0.43、Composer UIを刷新しエージェントとコミットメッセージ生成を追加
entries.titleEn: New Composer UI, Agent, Commit Messages
entries.summaryJa: Cursorはバージョン0.43で、Composerの新UIを導入するとともに、自律的にタスクを遂行するエージェント機能や、コミットメッセージの自動生成機能を追加した。開発体験の効率化を図るアップデートとなっている。
entries.summaryEn: Composer UI in the sidebar with inline diffs Early version of an agent in composer that can pick its own context and use the terminal Generation of git commit messages File pill recommendations in cha
entries.bodyJa:
AI搭載コードエディタCursorがバージョン0.43をリリースし、コード生成支援機能Composerの刷新と新しいエージェント機能、そしてGitコミットメッセージの自動生成機能を追加した。AIコーディングツール競争が激化する中で、ユーザー体験の改善と自律性の強化を狙った更新と位置づけられる。

中核となるのはComposerのUI刷新だ。Composerは複数ファイルにまたがるコード変更を対話的に行える機能で、今回のアップデートでは操作性や視認性の向上が図られたと見られる。加えて新登場の「Agent」は、ユーザーの指示に基づきファイル探索や編集、コマンド実行などを自律的に進めるモードと位置づけられており、単発の補完を超えてタスク単位でAIに作業を任せる流れに沿うものだ。

さらに、コミットメッセージを自動生成する機能も追加された。差分内容を解析し適切な要約文を提示することで、開発者の手間を減らす狙いがある。GitHub CopilotやJetBrains AI Assistantなどでも類似の機能が提供されており、AI支援開発における標準的な機能として定着しつつある領域だ。

背景として、Anthropicが発表したClaude向けの「computer use」やGitHubの「Copilot Workspace」、Devinなど、AIが自律的にタスクを完結させる「エージェント型」の流れが急速に広がっている。Cursorの今回のAgent追加もこの潮流に呼応するもので、コードエディタというユーザー接点を活かしながら、より長尺・複雑なタスクに踏み込もうとする戦略が読み取れる。実用上の精度や安全性については引き続き検証が必要だが、AIコーディングのワークフローが「補完」から「委任」へとシフトしていることを示すアップデートと言える。
entries.bodyEn:
Cursor has released version 0.43, introducing a redesigned UI for its multi-file code generation feature Composer, a new autonomous Agent mode, and automatic Git commit message generation. The release reflects an ongoing push by AI-assisted editors to deliver richer, more autonomous developer experiences.

The headline change is the Composer overhaul. Composer lets developers iterate on changes that span multiple files through a conversational interface, and the new UI appears aimed at improving clarity and flow when reviewing and applying AI-suggested edits. Alongside it, Cursor introduces an Agent capability that can take a higher-level instruction and autonomously navigate the codebase, edit files, and run commands to complete a task. This positions the editor closer to task-level delegation rather than line-by-line completion.

The update also adds a feature that drafts Git commit messages automatically, analyzing the staged diff and proposing a concise summary. Similar functionality has appeared in GitHub Copilot, JetBrains AI Assistant, and various IDE plugins, suggesting it is becoming a baseline expectation in AI-augmented development tooling rather than a differentiator on its own.

The broader context is the rapid rise of agentic coding tools. Anthropic's computer use API for Claude, GitHub's Copilot Workspace, Cognition's Devin, and a growing list of open-source agents such as OpenHands have all pushed the idea that an AI should be able to plan, execute, and verify multi-step engineering tasks rather than merely autocomplete code. Cursor, which has built a strong following among developers who want a tighter, native editor experience compared to chat-based assistants, seems to be leveraging its UI advantage to integrate these agent workflows directly into the place where code is written and reviewed.

It is worth noting that autonomous coding agents still face well-known limitations around reliability, context length, and the risk of confidently incorrect changes. How well Cursor's Agent handles larger repositories, ambiguous instructions, and recovery from mistakes will likely determine whether it becomes a daily-use feature or remains an occasional accelerator. Early adopters can be expected to test it on scoped refactors and boilerplate-heavy tasks before trusting it with sensitive production code.

Taken together, version 0.43 is an incremental but directionally significant release. The Composer redesign smooths an already popular workflow, the commit message helper trims a small but frequent friction point, and the Agent signals where Cursor — and arguably the AI coding category as a whole — is heading: from suggestion toward delegation.
